thread:
alex: heads up — we found a weird quota/usage accounting issue when the gateway does proto chunking for large responses. TL;DR: token/quota shows double the expected usage in the console :confused:

jin: curious — is this at the gateway boundary or in the runtime?

alex: gateway boundary. flow is client -> gateway (transcodes/merges) -> runtime. gateway splits big server-stream into 64k chunks, sends multipart to client. console aggregates bytes at gateway and again when runtime reports tokens. end result looks like duplicate accounting.

sophia: ugh. that will break per-route cost dashboards and any per-tenant billing. do we have a repro?

alex: yeah, repro attached in dm with curl. simple case: streaming embedding responses ~800kB. gateway chunker emits 13 chunks. console shows runtime tokens + gateway bytes.

kai: quick thought — are we conflating bytes and tokens? The runtime token counter is independent; gateway should only emit bytes for transfer metrics. We need a mapping layer that attributes only one of them to billing.

jin: agree. two options: (A) gateway tags forwarded traces with header `x-rw-attrib: runtime-only` so console dedups; (B) gateway emits a consolidated post-facto metric `gateway.output_aggregated_bytes` and we stop summing `gateway.chunks` + `runtime.tokens` in billing rollup.

ron: option A seems lower-lift, but fragile if third-party proxies strip headers. B is safer for long-term. Also consider sampling because we could increase metric cardinality.

alex: header approach example:

```
// gateway forwards
X-RW-ATTR: runtime-only
X-RW-TRACE-ID: 01abcd
```

alex: the runtime would still report tokens, console sees header on gateway metrics and skips gateway byte attribution for that trace id.

sophia: workable but race conditions possible if metrics arrive out of order. Also what about canary rollouts? we might route some small responses to new backend that doesn't emit the header. we need a fallback attribution rule.

kai: fallback: if header missing, dedupe by looking at `trace_id` join in the console. If both runtime.tokens and gateway.bytes exist for same trace_id within window (say 30s), prefer runtime.tokens for billing.

jin: that join will need accurate trace IDs end-to-end. Do we have consistent trace propagation across the sidecars? I thought some legacy clients still send `x-request-id` only.

ron: ops-bot: note — added task INF-482 to add trace-propagation test to smoke tests.

ops-bot: INF-482 created and assigned to @kai :rocket:

kai: ok we'll add the trace_id standardization middleware. but we should also fix telemetry UI so it surfaces these dedup rules — otherwise SREs panic.

sophia: agree. UI action items: show "attribution source" column (runtime | gateway | inferred) in per-route cost table, and tooltip with the dedupe heuristic used.

alex: perf note — the gateway chunking exists for browser streaming compat (sse/multipart). If we disable chunking to simplify accounting, some clients will time out. Not an option.

jin: could we instead add a compacting step that aggregates chunks into a single logical message for metrics only, without changing wire behavior? e.g., gateway emits `gateway.logical_message_size` once per response id.

kai: that's basically option B but spelled out. sounds good. small PR: gateway emit `logical_message_id` header on first chunk and `logical_message_complete` when done. console aggregates by logical_message_id.

ron: please keep the metric cardinality low — use histogram buckets for sizes, don't create a new high-cardinality gauge per request.

alex: ack. implementation sketch posted in thread GIST (dm).

jin: rollout plan: 1) implement logical_message_id metric (no billing change), 2) update console to show attribution and dedupe rules (beta flag), 3) after 2 has run for 2 weeks, flip billing logic to prefer runtime.tokens when logical_message_id present.

kai: canary strategy: route 5% of requests to gateway with logical ids and verify billing delta <1% and no spike in UI errors.

ron: add alert if dedup mismatch rate >0.5% for two consecutive minutes.

sophia: UX: add a small banner in console about "we dedupe gateway+runtime metrics for chunked responses" so customers understand discrepancies.

alex: last question — protobuf packing: some teams want to send packed repeated fields to reduce bytes. does that affect token accounting vs byte accounting?

jin: tokenization is runtime model-dependent, protobuf packing only affects wire bytes. token accounting stays with the runtime. but note: packed binary may compress better and reduce chunk count — so indirectly reduces gateway metrics.

kai: TL;DR: implement logical_message_id at gateway, standardize trace propagation, update console UX/metrics, canary, then flip billing. I'll open infra PRs today.

alex: thanks everyone — filing follow-ups for the console copy and the rollout doc. :thumbsup:
